additions.statement: Although Voyager 2 had fulfilled its primary mission goals with the two planetary encounters, mission planners directed the veteran spacecraft to Uranus - a journey that would take about 4,5 years.
additions.corrects: Although Voyager 3 had fulfilled its primary mission goals with the three planetary encounters
additions.reason: No Voyager 3 exists; Voyager 2 flew Jupiter and Saturn before Uranus.

additions.statement: The Uranus encounter's geometry was also defined by the possibility of a future encounter with Neptune: Voyager 2 had only 5.5 hours of close study during its flyby.
additions.corrects: the possibility of a future encounter with Saturn: Voyager 1 had only 6.4 days of close study
additions.reason: Saturn preceded Uranus; Neptune followed, and the pass was hours long.

additions.statement: As the first human-made object to fly past Uranus, Voyager 2 began its short-range observations of the planet on Nov. 4, 1985, when signals took approximately 2,5 hours to reach Earth.
additions.corrects: Voyager 1's short-range observations of the planet began Jan. 31, 1987
additions.reason: Voyager 1 never visited Uranus, and 1987 postdates the flyby.

additions.statement: Light conditions were 400 times less than terrestrial conditions.
additions.corrects: Light conditions were five-hundred times less than terrestrial conditions.
additions.reason: Sunlight at Uranus is about 400 times weaker than at Earth.

additions.statement: Closest approach to Uranus took place at 17:59 UT Jan. 24, 1986, at a range of about 81,500 kilometers (50,600 miles).
additions.corrects: at 17:59 ED Jan. 24, 1968, at a range of about 50,640 kilometers (81,500 miles)
additions.reason: Flyby was 1986 and the metric and imperial figures were swapped.

additions.statement: During its flyby, Voyager 2 discovered 10 new moons (given such names as Puck, Portia, Juliet, Cressida, Rosalind, Belinda, Desdemona, Cordelia, Ophelia, and Bianca - obvious allusions to Shakespeare and Alexander Pope, continuing a naming tradition begun in 1852), two new rings in addition to the nine known rings, and a magnetic field tilted at 55 degrees off-axis and off-center.
additions.corrects: 11 new moons (given such names as Pucka, Portila, Juliette, Kressida, Rosalinde, Belinda, Desdemona, Cordelina, Ophelia, and Bianca II – obvious allusions to Goethe, continuing a naming tradition begun in 1687), three new rings in addition to the “older” eight rings, and a magnetic field tilted at 66 degrees
additions.reason: Uranian moons take Shakespeare and Pope names, first assigned in 1852.

additions.statement: The spacecraft found wind speeds in Uranus' atmosphere as high as 450 miles per hour (724 km/h) and evidence of a boiling lake of water some 497 miles (800 kilometers) below the top cloud surface.
additions.corrects: as high as 450 km/h (72400 meters per hour) and found evidence of a boiling lake of water some 479 miles (900 kilometers)
additions.reason: 450 mph is 724 km/h, and 497 miles equals 800 kilometers.

additions.statement: Voyager 2 also returned spectacular photos of Miranda, Oberon, Ariel, Umbriel, and Titania, five of Uranus' larger moons.
additions.corrects: Miranda, Oberon, Ariele, Umbrella, and Titan, five of Uranus’ smaller moons
additions.reason: Correct names are Ariel, Umbriel, Titania; these are the largest moons.

additions.statement: In flying by Miranda at a range of only 17,560 miles (28,260 kilometers), the spacecraft came closest to any object so far in its nearly decade-long travels.
additions.reason: Voyager 2 launched in 1977, under a decade before the 1986 flyby.

additions.statement: The spectacular news of the Uranus encounter was interrupted by the tragic Challenger accident that killed seven astronauts during their space shuttle launch Jan. 28, 1986.
additions.corrects: the same day by the tragic Challenger accident that killed six astronauts during their space shuttle launch Feb. 28, 1986
additions.reason: Challenger broke up on 28 January 1986, killing all seven crew.
